## 2. Calibration (§4.3) — scan of the per-contact ratio

Exact scaling: with Coulomb excluded every term ∝ E₀ at fixed r = e₀·4πR_p²/E₀, so calibration exists iff f_He(r)/f_D(r) reaches the required ratio.

Regime: **contact** if the closest centroid pair is ≥ 1.3 fm (0.77 × 2R_p) and no skin point lies beyond 1.2 fm of its centroid, in both D and He-4; otherwise **engulfed** (one capsid wraps another — not a model of touching nucleons).

- 9.5 SUBDIV 4 convergence, 9.6 K_AREA doubled, 9.7 rotation: **not run** (no calibrated state to test; deferred).

## 6. Not run, and why

7.3 quartic mode (out-of-plane E(z)); 7.7 chain; the quadratic-fade variant; SUBDIV 4. Without a calibration these have no physical scale. The out-of-plane load path (§4) already bounds the out-of-plane stiffness: the first unstable force is below the 0.0125 MeV/fm resolution, i.e. the triangle gives no resistance out of plane, as the spec's §1 theorem says it must when there is no mesh/friction term.
